title: 报道：EA 关闭 BioWare，转而优先开发 Star Wars: Battlefront 续作

Report: EA shut down BioWare in favor of a Star Wars title
Business
Console
PC
News
Report: EA shut down BioWare in favor of Star Wars: Battlefront sequel after previously decrying licensed games
According to a new report, Electronic Arts closed down the venerated RPG studio BioWare to shift resources away from Mass Effect and toward a new Star Wars: Battlefront title.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
October 30, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
via DICE/EA
A new report indicatesElectronic Arts' r
ecent shutdown of BioWare
was precipitated by a financial showdown between two big science-fiction titles: the in-development Mass Effect: Universe and an unannounced new Star Wars: Battlefield title,
according to a new report from Bloomberg
. Unwilling to spend hundreds of millions of dollars on both projects, EA pivoted to putting its resources into Star Wars,
despite publicly shying away from licensed games
less than two years ago.
The Bloomberg report specifically cites financial pressure coming from the leveraged buy-out of Electronic Arts, which
saddled the company with $18 billion in debt
that it is expected to pay off that debt through operating profits. Trying to minimize losses and maximize returns, EA cancelled Mass Effect to focus on the less risky and more predictable wellspring of Star Wars with a new multiplayer-shooter Battlefront title.
Related:
Roblox growth slumps, but the company is betting big on AI to compensate
This decision comes just 18 months after EA cancelled an open-world Black Panther game and shut down developer
Cliffhanger Games
, and two years
after it announced
a strategic shift that took the company away from licensed titles. While a new Star Wars: Battlefront may fly in the face of that pivot, it is worth noting that EA's commitment to abandoning licensed titles was never full-bodied, as the company is still developing an Iron Man game based on the Marvel superhero.
The report also mentions that corporate politics may have played their own role in the closure, with EA shuffling around its executives and sidelining longtime EA Entertainment president Laura Miele, who had supported BioWare and Mass Effect in particular.
The cancellation of Mass Effect: Universe left BioWare in a lurch with no active projects, giving EA ample reason to shut the studio down.
In a recent interview with 80.lv
, BioWare co-founder Greg Zeschuk criticized the closure, stating that companies like EA do not understand game development.
?The other harsh reality of almost all these companies, the people that go down the business track never really come from the development track," Zeschuk said. “Because none of these people have ever made a game, like, never really sat and made one, like, from start to finish, even a small thing, they just don’t know how it works."
